subject: Post-call: Arcadia throughput & streaming clarifications
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Devon Price <devon@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Arcadia throughput & streaming clarifications

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and a focused set of asks so we can size capacity and validate SLOs before the technical deep-dive.

Summary of what we heard (please flag anything off):
- Primary use: document summarization + patient triage assistant in their provider portal (sync + streaming for long responses).
- Baseline QPS during business hours: ~10–15 requests/sec.
- Peak bursts: up to ~110–130 requests/sec for 30–90s windows (campaign spikes).
- Average input tokens/request we saw on call: ~700–1,100 (Devon said 900 avg).
- Streaming: majority of sessions are streaming responses with average stream duration ~20–30s and up to 20 simultaneous streams during peaks.
- Latency targets: p95 < 300ms for short responses; streaming chunk cadence ~200–500ms.

Asks (actionable, prioritized):
1) Devon: can you share a small workload sample (CSV) with timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_type (sync/stream), and an example of a peak-minute trace? A sanitized slice is fine — we just need distribution. If you have request traces (timestamps + client id + latency) that would be ideal.
2) Devon: confirm the SLOs you care about for both sync and streaming (p50/p95/p99 targets, and acceptable service degradation behavior during sustained bursts).
3) Marissa/Karthik/Neha: once we have the payload sample, can engineering run a quick mapping to: tokens/sec, sustained QPS required, concurrency for KV cache sizing, and a first-pass GPU slot estimate?
4) Operations: we'll need to map to two delivery options: Hosted (mixed-mode with autoscale) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) and estimate monthly cost deltas.

Attachments: I can accept a CSV attachment (arcadia_workload_sample.csv). I'm also attaching a short SOC2 evidence checklist request from Devon's compliance ask — Devon, sharing SOC/controls backlog helps speed enterprise procurement.

Next steps / timeline:
- Devon shares workload sample + SLO bullet list by Tue Nov 6.
- Redwood to return a capacity sketch and recommended delivery mode by Thu Nov 8.
- Schedule deep-dive (technical) for week of Nov 12 — propose Nov 9 10am PT if that works.

Thanks — rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment stubs: arcadia_workload_sample.csv (requested), SOC2_evidence_request.xlsx (attached stub)

From: Devon Price <devon@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@arcadiahealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Nov 2028 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Arcadia throughput & streaming clarifications

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the concise list. Attached is a small, sanitized sample of requests from last week's campaign (arcadia_workload_sample.csv). Quick notes from our side: 

- Baseline sustained QPS: 12 requests/sec (averaged over business hours).
- Peak: 125 requests/sec sustained for ~45–90s during our outreach campaigns; longer tails up to ~8 mins but at reduced QPS.
- Avg tokens per request (input): 900 tokens; avg tokens out: 1,100 tokens.
- Typical synchronous short responses: < 300 tokens, expected p95 < 200–250ms.
- Streaming behavior: longer summaries stream out in chunks — average 25s session length, chunk size ~150–300 tokens, chunk cadence 300–600ms.
- Concurrent streaming sessions during peak: 15–22 reported.
- Tolerance: We need functional availability; for critical triage flows we expect p95 < 350ms sync, and streaming chunk p99 delivery within 1.0s. If there is systematic degradation we need a clear fallback path (e.g., smaller model variant or text-only fallback).

I've attached arcadia_workload_sample.csv — columns: timestamp, client_id_hash, request_type, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms. Also attaching a short SOC2 evidence request (SOC2_evidence_request.xlsx) that procurement asked to start.

Happy to join the deep dive Nov 9 if that works; otherwise Nov 13 also open.

--
Devon Price
Director, Platform Integrations | Arcadia Health
devon@arcadiahealth.com

Attachment stubs: arcadia_workload_sample.csv (attached), SOC2_evidence_request.xlsx (attached)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Nov 2028 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Arcadia throughput & streaming clarifications

Thanks — received the sample and the latency targets. Quick internal plan and specific asks to engineering/ops: 

Snapshot from the CSV we looked at:
- Median tokens_in ~ 880, median tokens_out ~ 1,050.
- Peak-minute aggregate tokens/sec (from sample) ≈ 125 QPS * (900+1100) tokens ~= 250k tokens/sec at crest (worst-case burst).
- Sustained business-hour tokens/sec ≈ 12 QPS * 2000 tokens ~= 24k tokens/sec.

Initial sizing hypothesis (very rough):
- Hosted mixed-mode: autoscale that handles 12 QPS sustained with headroom for short bursts to 125 QPS using burst pool + prefix cache. Batching and KV cache should drop effective token/sec by ~20–35% for repeated contexts.
- Dedicated recommendation: reserve 2x of baseline throughput (for predictable latency), with burst capacity configured via reserved burst slots or on-demand GPU pool. We'll quantify exact GPU slots after Karthik runs the perf mapping.

Karthik / Neha, asks:
1) Run a quick mapping: tokens/sec -> slot sizing (NVIDIA 80GB-equivalent) assuming Redwood midsize quantization and streaming overheads; include memory for KV cache for 20 concurrent streams. Use 95th p95 latency target of 300ms as the performance goal. Use this sheet: capacity-estimate-template.xlsx (attached).
2) Flag model variant suggestions: smaller/cheaper variant for fallback so procurement has clear cost delta.
3) Note: procurement will want SOC2 artifacts — I'll own the response to SOC2_evidence_request.xlsx. Devon, I'll loop your security contact if we need clarifications.

I'll take the draft slot estimates and produce a short 'Hosted vs Dedicated' delta for the Nov 8 deliverable.

Marissa
